words.eg: {Sorry to bother you}, but is this the queue for the desk?
words.clue: La formule d’ouverture par défaut avec un inconnu.

words.eg: That was entirely {my fault} and I should have checked.

words.fr: il n’y a pas de mal
words.eg: Do not worry about it — {no harm done}.
{I do apologise}, the message went to the wrong address.
{Thanks a lot}, that has saved me an afternoon.
Sent it over this morning — {much appreciated}.
Oh, {you shouldn’t have} — and I am very glad you did.
Let me buy the next one to {make up for} last week.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces formules servent à s’excuser. Laquelle sert à réparer ?
odd.why: Se rattraper vient après l’excuse, et coûte quelque chose.

words.eg: {Would you mind} shutting the window, it is freezing.

no.would you mind to: Après « would you mind », le verbe prend -ing : « would you mind shutting », jamais « to shut ».

words.eg: {Could you possibly} send it before five?
{Is it all right if} I take Friday off?
{Feel free to} say no, it is genuinely fine.
{How about} Thursday instead?
{Why don’t we} do it before the meeting rather than after?
{If you get a chance}, have a look at the second page.
{By all means}, take the whole file.
{As far as I’m concerned}, it was settled a month ago.
{I’d say} it takes three weeks, not two.
{Fair enough}, I had not thought of it that way.
words.clue: L’expression qui clôt une objection sans donner tout à fait raison.

words.fr: je vois ce que vous voulez dire
words.eg: {I take your point}, but the dates do not move.
That is true {up to a point}, and then it stops being true.
{To be honest}, nobody read it before it went out.

words.fr: permettez-moi de ne pas être d’accord
words.eg: {I beg to differ}, and I have the numbers here.

words.en: that’s one way of putting it
words.fr: c’est une façon de voir les choses
words.eg: {That’s one way of putting it}, and it is not mine.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces formules répondent à quelqu’un. Laquelle ouvre ?
odd.why: « I’d say » lance un avis ; les trois autres réagissent à celui d’un autre.

words.eg: {I’m not keen on it}, but I will go if everyone else is.
Cricket {is not my thing} and I have tried twice.
{I’d rather} walk than wait twenty minutes for a bus.

no.I would rather to: Après « would rather », le verbe reste nu : « I’d rather walk », jamais « to walk ».

words.eg: {I can’t stand it} when people reply without reading.
{I don’t mind} either way, you choose.
He is genuinely {fond of} that terrible old car.
The city {grows on} you, everyone says so and everyone is right.
Pub or the flat — {I’m easy}.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces formules disent qu’on n’aime pas. Laquelle dit le contraire ?
odd.why: « To grow on you » décrit un goût qui vient avec le temps.

words.eg: {Are you all right?} is a greeting here, not a question about your health.
words.clue: Piège absolu : ce n’est pas de l’inquiétude, c’est bonjour.

words.eg: {How’s it going?} — and the answer is « not bad », whatever the truth.
{Long time no see} — you have not changed a bit.
Right, {see you in a bit}.
{Take care} — and let me know how it goes.
{Cheers} works as thank you, as goodbye, and as a toast.
words.clue: Le mot le plus utile du pays : trois sens, aucun effort.

words.eg: {All the best} — and do come back and see us.
{Give my regards to} your mother when you see her.

odd.prompt: Trois de ces formules servent à partir. Laquelle sert à arriver ?
odd.why: « Long time no see » se dit en se retrouvant.
